analysis:
This PR changes documentation only (docs/developer/test.md and docs/provider/cli-reference.md); no executable code, protocol, or trust-boundary behavior is modified in the supplied evidence. I examined the head_text for test.md (lines 480-1150) and the full cli-reference.md patch. The documented changes describe a new advisory GLM-5.3-Flash wired-memory diagnostic: a doctor check, a start warning, a status fix line and a daemon log notice. They also describe a new 0600 `~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json` file (`VerifiedWeightHashStore`) that caches managed GLM load hashes bound to file identities and reuses them for startup registration, and a variable-frame-rate video note.

Security-relevant observations for integration. First, the verified-weights store relates to A-004, T-012 and T-027: weight-hash integrity is reported to the coordinator via a cached hash. The source (`VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift`) is not in this batch, so whether the file-identity binding (size, mtime, inode) resists an operator swapping weights after verification cannot be confirmed. That is inherent to the operator-adversary model in TB-003 and is documented as bound to file identities. The code should be reviewed where it lands. Second, the docs state that the error text is only matched, never logged, and that the new diagnostics do not change admission, KV grants or capacity. This is consistent with A-001 and T-008 and cannot be verified from docs alone. Third, the sudo LaunchDaemon heredoc install instructions are user-run guidance and add no new attack surface in the docs themselves. Fourth, the test docs make no changes to the T-041 cache posture; they reference isolated ephemeral keys and warn never to use production cache roots or keys.

No concrete regression or threat-model invalidation is evident from the documentation. Code-level verification of the referenced Swift sources is outside the supplied evidence.
